2. During the course of scrutiny of these Orders, the Committee has noted 
some cases where there has been a cons iderable time lag between the date of 
notification of the Order and the date of its laying. The annexed statement also 
indicates the period of dela y in cases where notifications  have not been laid as 
per the schedule prescribed by the Committee and where such notifications 
were accompanied by a statement indicating the reasons for the delay in laying. 
In some of the cases the delay has been quite long. The 
observations/recommendations of the Co mmittee in respect of the specific 
Ministries/Departments are as follows: -    
  
(i) Ministry of Communication  and Information Technology 
 (Department of Posts) 
 
Ministry of Communication and In formation Technology (Department 
of Posts) have laid 3 notifications. One notification (Sl. No. 20) has been 
delayed by 1 year and 3 months and ha s delay statement at tached with it. 
Explaining the reasons of delay, the Ministry has stated as under:- 

 
 
 “The copies of the Gazette Notification which was published in the 
Gazette of India Extraordinary, Part II – Section 3, sub section (i) vide No. 626 
dated October 29, 2009 regarding introduc tion of Overnight Parcel Service 
could not be laid on the Ta ble of Rajya Sabha due to the fact the service could 
not be launched due to rescheduling of the India Post freighters being operated 
by Air India. The notification is now being laid on the table of the Rajya Sabha 
during the Budget Session of Parliament.” 
 
The Committee have noted the reply  given by the Ministry of 
Communication and Information Tec hnology (Department of Posts) and 
hope that the Ministry would take  adequate precaution to avoid such 
delays in future. 
 
(ii) Ministry of Defence 
 
 Ministry of Defence have laid 2 not ifications (Sl. Nos. 39 and 40). Out 
of these one notification (Sl. No. 39) is delayed by 5 months and  no  delay 
statement  is attached  thereto. 
  
  The Committee urges the Ministry of Defence to append the delay 
statement where there is delay in laying of notifications and avoid 
recurrence of such delays in future. 
 
(iii) Ministry of Environment and Forests 
 
 Ministry of Environment and Forest s have laid 14 not ifications (Sl. 
Nos. 41 to 54). 5 notifications have been delayed. The delay period ranges 
from 5 months to 1 year. No delay statement has been attached to any of these 
delayed notifications. 
 
The Committee in the absence of de lay statements are not able to 
know the reasons behind this del ay. Therefore, the Committee invite 
attention to its recommendation contained in its 131
st R e p o r t   i n  t h i s  
connection where it is observed to append invariably delay statement in 
case of delay in laying of notifications by  the Ministry. 
 
(iv)   Ministry of Finance 
 
 (A)  (Department of Financial Services) 
 
 The Ministry of Finance (Departmen t of Financial Services) have laid 
14 notifications (Sl. Nos. 72 – 85). Out of these 5 notifications have been 
delayed and no delay statements  is appended to them. The delay period ranges 
from 4 months to 10 months. 
 

 
 The Committee takes note of the fact and advices Ministry of 
Finance (Department of Financial Servi ces) shall ensure timely laying of 
their notifications as per th e schedule prescribed in its 131 st Report. 
Therefore,  the Committee reiterate its directed that the Ministry should  
keep the Parliament informed of the reasons of delay in laying of their 
subordinate legislation.  
 
(B)  (Department of Revenue) 
 
 The Ministry of Finance (Department of Revenue) have laid 117 
notifications out of  which 20 notifications (Sl. Nos. 86-92, 101-103, 138-139, 
154-160 & 177) have been delayed. The delay ranges from 3 to 5 months. The 
Ministry have failed to append delay statement to any of them. 
  
 
 The Committee invite attention to  its recommendations made in 
135
th Report, wherein it is laid down that it is essential to append a 
statement in case of delay in laying  of statutory orders. The Committee 
therefore, impress upon the Ministry of Finance (Department of Revenue) 
to append delay statement in case of any delay and strictly adhere to the 
time schedule in laying of notifications so as to avoid any delay in laying of 
notifications. 
 
(v) Health and Family Welfare 
 
  The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare have laid 13 notifications
 
on the Table of the House. 7 notifications have been delayed. Out of these  3 
notifications which have been delayed have no delay statements appended to 
them. 4 notifications  have been accompanied by delay statements. The delay 
period ranges from 4 months to 1 year . The reasons given by the Ministry is 
that it took some time to complete the procedural formalities and therefore, 
papers could not be laid in time. 
 
 The Committee are not convinced of the vague reasons of delay 
given by the Ministry of Health a nd Family Welfare that due to time 
taken by the procedural formalitie s, the Ministry could not lay the 
notifications in time. If, it was so, th e Ministry should have foreseen the 
things beforehand and would have acted  promptly. The Committee 
castigate this lackadaisical approach by  the Ministry and advise them to 
take care in future in laying of notifications.  
 
(vi)      Ministry of Home Affairs  
 
The Ministry of Home Af fairs have laid 25 notifications out of which 
11 notifications have been delayed. The delay period ranges from 4 months to 
1 year. Eight notifications (Sl. Nos. 217-219, 221, 225, 228-229 and 235) have 

 
no delay statement attached. Three no tifications have delay statement 
appended. The reasons forwarded by the Ministry for delay is as under:- 
 
“The Daman & Diu Private Security Agencies Rules, 2009 were 
notified by the UT Administration of Daman & Diu vide Notification 
No. 1/DC/Home/7/DDPSAR/2009-2010/42 dated 18.9.2009 for 
carrying out the provisions of the Private Security Agencies 
(Regulation) Act, 2005. As per Sec tion 25($) of the Act, the above 
Rules are proposed to be laid before  both Houses of Parliament during 
the current Monsoon Session of Parliament. 
The UT Administration had expe ditiously notified and printed 
the English version of the Rule s on 21.8.2009. Translation of the Rules 
into Hindi, however, took considerable time and the UT Administration 
was able to publish the Hindi version in November, 2009. This coupled 
with other administrative reasons re sulted in delay in laying of the 
aforesaid Rules before each House of Parliament”. 
 
 The Committee take serious note of the fact that delay was caused 
due to administrative reasons. Ministries have been taking recourse to this 
plea very frequently. This possibility   should have been assessed well 
before and adequate arrangements sh ould have been made in respect 
thereof. The Committee advises the Minist ry of Home Affairs to take care 
so that such delays do not recur in future. 
 
(vii) Ministry of Human Resource Development 
  
 (Department of Higher Educat ion & Department of School 
Education and Literacy) 
 
The Ministry of Human Resource De velopment (Department of Higher 
Education) have laid 5 notifications (Sl. Nos. 242-246). Out of these 3 
notifications have been delayed, 2 no tifications have no delay statement 
appended with them and only 1 notif ication is accompanied with delay 
statement. The delay period ranges from  5 months to 1 year and 11 months. 
The Ministry have given reason for de lay as non-availabili ty of requisite 
number of printed copies from the Press. 
   
  Department of School Education and L iteracy have laid 2 notifications 
and both of these have been delayed by 3 months and no delay statement is 
appended thereto. 
 
  The Committee are not happy over th e inordinate delay extending 
upto about 2 years in laying of some of these notifications. Further the 
reasons given such as non-availability of requisite number of printed 
copies appear to be lame excuse. The Committee therefore, impress upon  
the Ministry to  devise suitable mechanism to avoid such instances of delay 

 
in future and in case of  any delay in laying,  a delay statement should 
invariably be appended. 
 
 (viii) Ministry of Power 
 
 The Ministry of Power have laid  21 notifications out of  which 5 
notification have delayed, 4 notifications (Sl. Nos. 309-312) have been delayed 
by 1 year and these have no delay statement appended with them. One 
notification (Sl. No. 304) has delay period of  4 months and is attached with  
delay statement. The reason for delay given by the Ministry is as under:- 
 
 “The Regulation was published in the Gazette of India Extraordinary 
dated 23
rd October, 2009 and printed copies of the same were received by the 
Central Electricity Regulatory Commission only on 18 th December, 2009 from 
the Press. Copies of the Regulation were  received in the Mi nistry of Power on 
18th December, 2009. The House was adjourned on 21.12.2009. since only one 
day was available before the House was adjourned, the Regulation could not be 
laid in the winter session 2009.” 
  
 The Committee observe that sessions are declared much in advance 
and had the Ministry of Power take n prompt steps for laying of the 
notifications, the delay could have  been avoided. It reflects the bad 
management planning on the part  of the Ministry. The Committee, 
therefore,  recommend that the Ministry should take the first available 
opportunity for laying of their notifications during the session. 
 
 
(ix)     Ministry of Road Transport & Highways 
 
 The Ministry of Road Transport & Highways have laid 317 
notifications
 on the Table of the House. Out of  these 102 notif ications have 
been delayed. All of these have no de lay statements appended thereto and  
delay period ranges from 3 months to 8 months.  
  
 The Committee take note of the fact that Ministry of Road 
Transport and Highways have done mammoth work in laying such huge 
volume of notifications on the table of the House.  The Committee 
however regret that the Ministry h ave not appended any delay statement 
with any delayed Notifications. Ministry of Road Transport and Highways 
should see or look into the matter seriously to eliminate recurrence of such 
delays in future. 
 
 
 
 

 
(x) Ministry of Science and Technology (Department of Science and 
Technology) 
 
 The Ministry of Science and Technology (Department of Science and 
Technology) have laid only one notification (Sl. No. 630) which has been 
delayed by 4 months. The Ministry have  appended delay statement with the 
notification and the reasons given by the Ministry is as under:- 
 
 “As per section 22 of the Scien ce and Engineering Research Board 
(SERB) Act, 2008 (9 of 2009), the Scie nce and Engineering Research Board 
Rules is required to be laid on the Table of Lok Sabha/Rajya Sabha. Though 
the papers pertaining to SERB rules were  sent to the Parliament Secretariat 
during the last Parliament session, in advertently, the papers regarding 
enforcement of the Act (No. G.S.R. 212 (E) dated the 29
th March, 2010) were 
laid on the table of both the Houses, in stead of SERB Rules (Notification No. 
G.S.R. 213 (E) dated the 29 th March, 2010). Hence the delay in laying the 
papers in respect of the SERB Rules.” 
 
 The Committee have noted the rep ly given by the Ministry of 
Science and Technology (Department of  Science and Technology) and 
hope that the Ministry will adh ere strictly to the schedule as 
recommended by the Committee for timely laying of Subordinate 
Legislation so that such lapses do not recur in future. 
 
 
(xi) Ministry of Shipping 
  
The Ministry of Shipping  have la id 5 notifications ( Sl. Nos. 631-635) 
out of which 2 notifications have been  delayed. The delay period ranges  from 
3 to 5 months and both of them have delay statements appended. The reasons 
for delay  given by the Ministry is  that the time taken to  get sufficient number 
of printed copies caused delay. 
  
 The Committee find that the reply given by the Ministry as to the 
reasons of delay is not convincing a nd appears to be evasive. Delay could 
be avoided, had precaution been taken by  the Ministry in this regard. The 
Committee hope that the Ministry of Shipping would cut on such delays in 
future particularly on account of de lay in receiving printed copies of 
notifications by evolving and effective mechanism and would adhere to the 
time schedule as prescribed in Committee’s 131
st Report. 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 
(xii) Ministry of Textiles 
 
 The Ministry of Textiles have laid  2 notifications (Sl. Nos. 636-637) 
one of which (Sl. No. 636) has been delayed. The delay ranges upto 3 months 
and no delay statement has been attached. 
 
 The Committee impress upon the Mini stry of Textiles to evolve 
suitable mechanism to avoid such de lays and also to append delay 
statements where there has been a delay, in laying of notification. 
  
3. The Committee impresses upon all the Ministries/Departments to take 
immediate steps to ensure timely and pr oper laying of subordinate legislation. 
The Committee, accordingly, wishes to bring to the notice of all 
Ministries/Departments of the Government of India, particularly, the defaulting 
ones, the following recommendations, as contained in its 131
st
,135
th and 152nd 
Reports: 
 
 “Orders required to be laid before the House should be laid (i) if the 
House is not in Session, during the Se ssion immediately following the date 
of publication of the Order in the Offici al Gazette and (ii) if the House is 
in Session, on the date of the pub lication of the Order, during its 
continuance and in case the time l ag between the date of publication and 
the date of the closing of the Session is less than 15 clear days, before the 
expiry of the Session immediately following the said Session. All the 
Ministries/Departments of Governme nt of India should henceforth 
comply with this schedule in the matt er of laying of the Orders issued 
under various Acts of Parliament on the Table of the Rajya Sabha. 
(131st Report) 
(Presented on 15 December 2000) 
 
 “The Committee has, time and again,  emphasized that it is essential 
that in case there is a delay in th e laying of Statutory Orders, the 
concerned Ministry/Department should invariably append a delay 
statement along with the notificati ons being laid so as to apprise 
Parliament of the causes of delay. The Committee desires all 
Ministries/Departments to take a note of this, since the intension is that 
through the process of formulation of a delay statement the Ministry is 
able to introspect, identify bottlenecks and devise remedial measures”. 
(135th Report) 
(Presented on 27 July 2001) 
 

 
 “In the opinion of the Committee,  every notification should be 
assigned a distinctive number in order to give it a separate identity and 
similarly, no notification should be published/laid which does not carry a 
notification number. The Committee ex pects all Ministries/Departments 
of Government of India to exercise caution in this regard. In case where 
there are more than one notification under a single file, the 
Ministries/Departments should ensu re that the file number on each 
notification should be suitably distinguished from one another. 
(152
nd
 Report)

PARLIAMENT OF INDIA 
RAJYA SABHA 
 
COMMITTEE ON SUBORDINATE LEGISLATION 
 
HUNDRED AND NINETY ONE REPORT 
 
ON 
 
(i) The Railways (Punitive Charges for Overloading of Wagon) Rules, 2007;  
 
and 
 
(ii) The Delhi Advocate's Welfare Fund Rules, 2001-Implementation of 169th 
Report of the Committee on Subordinate Legislation 
 
 
                                  (Presented on 16TH March, 2011) 
 
 
 
 
 
 
                                RAJYA SABHA SECRETARIAT 
                                              NEW DELHI 
 
             March, 2011/ Phalguna,1932  (Saka) 
191  

 
(I)  
The Railways (Punitive charges for overloading of wagon) Rules, 2007 
 
 
 The Railways (Punitive c harges for overloading of wagon ) Rules, 
2007 (Annexure-I) framed under the Railways Act, 1989 (Annexure-II) were 
notified on 15.06.2007. 
  
2. The main objective  to notify these rules was  to check overloading  of 
wagons and to ensure safe train operation as overloading of wagons 
endangers  the safety of the wagon and track.  As loading in railway wagons 
cannot b e precisely controlled, provision of loading tolerance have been 
made in the rules.  Besides, these rules also intend to check revenue leakage 
caused by understating of weight of consignment loaded in railway wagons. 
To overcome the menace of overloading rules of punitive charges have been 
made stringent for those rail users who have malafide intention. 
The operational benefit of these rules is that it ensure safe train operation 
and prevent leakage of revenue. 
 
3.  The Ministry has informed in th eir background note (Annerxure- III) 
that the incidence of overloading, in case of  West Central and East Central 
for a particular month of 2008 in comparison to corresponding mont h of 
2007 has decreased due to levy of punitive charges for overloading. The 
incidence of overloaded wagons in West Central Railway has reduced to 
10.6% from 22.08% whereas in East Central Railway it has reduced to 
4.76% from 11.28% 
 

4.  The Railway s (Punitive charges for overloading of wagon)  Rules, 
2007 framed under the Railway s  Act, 198 9 were examined and a 
questionnaire on the subject was forwarded to the Ministry of Railways for 
their comments/clarifications on 16 th May, 2008.  The Ministry furnished 
their comments/clarifications on 16th June, 2008 (Annexure IV). 
 
5.  On the query that  what changes took place at the ground level that 
necessitated the supersession of the Rules of 2005 and what are the salient 
features of the new set of rules’ and what loop -holes in the previsous rules 
have been plugged through the new rules?  The Ministry replied that: 
“After the issue of Railways (Punitive charges for overloading of wagon ) 
Rules, 2006 following changes took place: 
 The concept of charging of freight on the basis of CC commodities 
and Enhanced CC commodities was done way with w.e.f 01.03.0 7.  
The freight was chargeable on the basis of permissible carrying of the 
wagons. 
 Loading tolerance  of 1 tonne was provided for all covered wagons 
and BOY/ BOYN tolerance of wagons and loading tolerance of 2 
tonnes was provided for all other wagons (except  covered and 
BOY/BOYN wagons) 
 The above changes necessitated for the amendments in the Railways 
(Punitive charges for overloading of Wagons) Rules, 2006.  Therefore, in 
supersession of Rules of 2006, Railways (Punitive charges for overloading 
of Wagons) Rules, 2007 were notified on 15.6.2007. 
Salient features of Railways (Punitive charges for overloading of Wagons) 
Rules, 2007 are as under: 

 Punitive charges are levied wagon-wise for all commodities instead of 
‘CC’ & ‘Enchanced CC’ comm odities wise as was e arlier in Rules of 
2006. 
 Loading tolerance of 2 tonnes have been provided for all type of 
commodities.  BOY, BOYN, covered, Tank wagons and container 
trains are exceptions in which loading tolerance is one tonne. 
 Graded punitive charges, as prevalent earlier have been retained. 
 There was no loop -holes in the  previous Rules of 2006.  But as the 
system of charging of freight had undergone a change, the rules for punitive 
charges for overloading accordingly needed a corresponding change which 
has been done with the issue of Rules of 2007”. 
 
6.  The Committee wanted to know that the rationale behind levying 
punitive charges three times of the freight rate applicable to the highest class 
in case of overloading by more than five tonnes while provision already 
exists of levying two times of the freight rate in case of overloaded by more 
than two tones for eight wheeled wagons ( except BOX and BOST wagons) 
why the same rules are not applicable in case of BOX and BOST and all 
other types of wagons and for container tr ain where the weight of the 
commodity exceeds the permissible carrying capacity of the wagon; punitive 
charges leviable is two times of the freight rate in case of overloading by 
more than one tonne but not more than four tones and three times of the 
freight rate in case of overloading by more than four tones.  Whether rules 
should not uniformly be applicable in all cases.  On this the Ministry 
informed the Committee that: 
“In the rules of 2006, in case of BOX and BOST wagons, loading tolerance 
of one tonne  was provided.  But the concept of charging of freight on the 

basis of CC commodities and Enhanced CC commodities was done way with 
w.e.f. 01.03.07.  The freight was chargeable on the basis of permissible 
carrying of the wagons.  Loading tolerance of 1 tonne was providees for all 
covered wagons and Boy BOYN  wagons and loading tolerance of 2 tonnes 
was provided for all other wagons (except covered and BOY/BOYN 
wagons).  Accordingly, Railways (Punitive charges for overloading of 
wagons) Rules, 2007 were notified on 15.06.2007. 
 A need was felt to introduce graded punitive charges for varying 
quantity of overloading.  It was decided  to levy less punitive charges when 
overloading was less and to impose higher punitive charges when extent of 
overloading was much.   Therefore, in case of wagons other than covered, 
tank and BOY/BOYN wagons when the weight exceeds of PCC of the 
wagons by more than 2 tonnes but up to 5 tonnes (l oading tolerance, i.e., 2 
tonnes + 3 tonne), punitive charges  @ 2 times of freight rate appl icable to 
commodity is levied, whereas when the weight exceeds the PCC of the 
wagons by more than 5 tonne s, when punitive charges @ 3 times of the 
freight rate applicable to the highest class, is levied. 
 In ideal conditions, the rails user  is expected to load the wagons upto 
the prescribed Permissible  Carrying Capacity (PCC) of wagon.  However, 
overloading cannot be controlled up to the PCC because of certain practical 
situations.  In order to take  care of eventuality of overloading more than 
PCC, a loadi ng tolerance of 1 tonne/2 tonne has been prescribed.  For all 
other types of wagons like open wagons which are more prone to 
overloading, the loading tolerance of 2 tonne has been prescribed. 
 Due to difference in loading tolerance the slabs of rates for p unitive 
charges are different.  In case where loading tolerance has been  prescribed 
as 2 tonnes, the slabs are upto 2 tonnes, between 2 tonnes and 5 tonnes and 

more than 5 tonnes.  In case of loading tolerance has been prescribed as 1 
tonne, the slabs are  upto 1 tonne, between 1 tonne and 4 tonnes, and more 
than 4 tonnes.” 
 
7.  The Committee observed that there are rules/provision made for three 
types of overloading as mentioned under Par t I, II and III whereas in the 
Rules of 2006, these were covered unde r Part I and II only; what are the 
reasons for adding additional Part III under the new rules Regarding this  the 
Ministry clarified that a separate part has been added to specifically mention 
container trains to made the provisions more clear.  In the ear lier rules, it 
was covered under Part-II. 
8.  The Committee wanted to know to what extent, these rules would 
work as deterrent in so far as overloading of wagons is concerned . On this 
issue the Ministry informed that the rules for punitive charges for 
overloading have been made to act as a deterrent in overloading of wagons.  
Overloading of wagons not only endangers safety, but results in leakage of 
revenue.  It is expected that these rules will be effective in checking the 
overloading of wagons. 
9.  On the  querry whether any difference have been witnessed over 
revenue collection since introduction of the Railway ( Punitive charges for 
overloading of wagon) Rules, 2007,    the Ministry informed that the main  
rationale for levying the punitive charges for  overloading is to ensure saf e 
train operation and to check overloading by way of penalty.  These charges 
are not viewed as source of revenue.  These are treated as part of freight and 
are recoverable with the freight.  Railways do not maintain separate accounts 
for punitive charges.   

 The Ministry further stated that t hese rules were revised in 2007 due 
to circumstances necessitation these changes.  These rules were not modified 
as a measure of generation of revenue. 
 
10.  On the query that whether the Ministry  is contemplating punitive 
charges from all consumers/stakeholders involved  in overloading be it 
intentional; if not, how these rules will be applicable for both the parties.  
The Ministry stated that the p unitive charges for overloading are levied on 
all rail users if excess weight is found.  However, different rates are charged 
depending upon the extent of overloading, and actual payload in comparison 
with combined Permissible Carrying Capacity (PCC) of the rake. 
11. The Committee sought clarifications on the issue that punitive charges 
leviable on the the commodity  weighing  more than one tonne is two times 
the freight  rates applicable to that commodity,   whether these charges are  
high and stringent   On this the Ministry stated that the Railways are of th e 
view that current structure of rates of punitive charges is reasonable.  This 
structure is constantly reviewed on the basis of feed back received from the 
Zonal Railways and rail-users. 
12.  The Committee observed that the Rules do not mention the maximu m 
limit of overloading in a wagon beyond which detachments of overloaded 
wagons for off -loading should invariably be done.   The Ministry informed 
that the maximum permissible weight which is equal to PCC of the wagon  
plus loading tolerance, has been  prescribed in respect of all wagons.  A rail -
user is expected  to load within this limit only.  Any variation in the loaded 
weight6 on account of justifiable reasons has been taken care of by way of 
loading tolerance. 

 However, the wagons, which are found overloa ded on weighment, 
may be detached/adjusted or run with restricted speed based on the rail -
infrastructure which varies from Railway to Railway.  All Zonal Railways 
have made a procedure order for dealing with overloaded wagons, which 
includes provisions regarding detachment. 
 
13.  The Committee wanted to know  whether it would not be appropriate 
if Punitive Charges are borne by the sender and not by the consignee in 
order to fight the menace of overloading; otherwise, the burden gets 
transferred to the consignee and through him to the consumer Regarding this 
the Ministry commented that  as per extant rules, a rail -user that makes the 
payment of freight is required to pay the punitive charges also.  All 
consignments are required to be weighed at weighbridges bef ore issue of 
Railway Receipt and efforts are made to include punitive charges in Railway 
Receipts itself. 
However, if the punitive charges cannot be included in Railway Receipt 
itself due to any reason, the same is to be realized from the consignee. 
 
Recommendations 
14.  The Committee is of the opinion that the R ules should reflect the 
maximum limit of overloading in a wagon beyond  which  detatchment 
of overloaded wagons for off loading or detatchment should be done. 
15.  The Committee is of the view in cas e of overload on weighment 
what would be the restricted speed based on the rail -infrastructure on 
which the wagons  would run and the maximum overload  on 
weightment till which it would allow to run should be categorically 
mentioned in the Rules. 

16.  The Committee suggests that the Rules for punitive charges for 
overloading should aim at not only reducing the overloading but also at 
reducing at a successive rate every year reducing loading tolerance. 
17.  The Committee recommends that the punitive charges f or 
overloading wagons can be modi fied as a measure of generation of 
revenue as overloading of wagons not only endangers safety but results 
in leakage of revenue also. 
 
 
 

II 
Delhi Advocate’s Welfare Fund Rules, 2001-Implementation of the 169th Report of 
the Committee 
 
 
 The Delhi Advocate’s Welfare Fund Rules, 2001 framed under the Advocate’s 
Welfare Fund Act, 2001, were examined and the matter was reported in the 169 th Report 
of the Committee presented to the House on the 5 th September, 2007.  In the Report, the 
Committee had recommended/ observed as under: 
 
“2. The Committee notes with satisfaction that the Ministry of Law & Justice 
(Department of Legal Af fairs) have react ed favorably on the various points that 
were referred to them for comments/clarificat ions. The Committee notes that the 
Ministry have agreed to take action as follows in pursuance to its recommendations: 
 
 Point 1 (Rule 9 (8)):   To provide that the Chairperson presiding over the 
meeting, exercises his voting right only in cases where there  is a tie in the 
votes cast, for the purpose of resolution of the same. 
  
Point 3 (Rule 12(1)):  (i) To provide a specific time period of 4 months for 
issuing a certificate for recognition in Form- IV. 
 (ii) To provide for an authority for appeal/ review , if the application for 
recognition is rejected, which may be the State Bar Council of each State. 
  
Point 5 (Rule 14):  (i) To prescribe 6 months as the period for seeking re -
admission as a member of the fund and by fixing the interest on arrears at 
the time of re-admission at not exceeding 3%. 
 (ii) To prescribe a period of 15 days to ensure continuity of the membership 
of the fund and that the membership may be discontinued , if the member 
failed to respond. 
  
Point 6 (Rule 15 ):  To prescribe 6 months perio d for the issuance of 
certificate of membership to the fund. 
  
Point 7 (Rule 16):  To increase the period from 15 to 45 days for intimating 
the removal/ suspension of a member from the State roll to the Trustee 
Committee. 
  
Point 8 (Rule 19): To substitute the word 'thiery' with the word 'thirty', 
thereby rectifying a typographical error.  
 
On rest of the points the Committee accepts the explanation furnished by the 
Ministry. 
 

 The Committee, however recommends that the Ministry of Law and Justice 
should carry out modification in the Rules as agreed to by them, expeditiously.” 
 
 
 2. Relevant extracts from the 169th Report were forwarded to the Ministry of Law & 
Justice (Department of Legal Affairs) for necessary action on the 14th September, 2007.   
 
3. The M inistry of Law & Justice (Department of Legal Affairs) vide their 
communication dated the 11 th October, 2007 informed that  relevant extracts of the  
Report had been forwarded to the Department of Law, Justice & Legislative Affairs of 
the Government of Nati onal Capital Territory of Delhi for carrying out the amendments 
in the Rules in pursuance to the Committee’s recommendations.  The powers of the 
Central Government for framing rules under Section 35 of the Advocate’s Welfare Fund 
Act, 2001 has been delegat ed to the Administrators of the Union territories and the 
Government of NCT of Delhi in pursuance of which the Government of NCT of Delhi 
had framed the Delhi Advocates’ Welfare Fund Rules, 2001.    
  
4. The Department of Law, Justice & Legislative Affairs of the Government of NCT 
of Delhi vide their communication dated the 3 rd June, 2009 has furnished a copy of the 
notification No. F.219/litigation/01/Dysecylaw/1932 -51 dated the 8 th May, 2009 
publishing the Delhi Advocate’s Welfare Fund (Amendment) Rules, 2009 (Annexure).   
 
5. The Committee notes with satisfaction that the Government of NCT of Delhi  
has carried amendments in the Delhi Advocate’s Welfare Fund Rules, 2001 
incorporating its suggestions/ recommendations in: 
 
 (i) Rule 9 (8) by providing that the Chairperson presiding over the meeting, 
exercises his voting right only in case  there is a tie in the votes cast, for 
the purpose of resolution of the same; 
 
 (ii) Rule 12(1) by providing a specific time period of 4 months for issuing a 
certificate for  recognition in Form - IV and also  by providing for an 

authority for appeal/ review , if the application for recognition is rejected 
which may be the State Bar Council of each State; 
(iii) Rule 14 by prescribing  6 months as the period for seeking re -admission 
as a member of the fund and by fixing the interest on arrears at the time 
of re -admission at not exceeding 3% and  by prescribing  a period of 15 
days to ensure continuity of the membership of the fund and that the 
membership may be discontinued if the member failed to respond; 
 
(iv) Rule 15 by prescribing 6 months period for the issuance of certif icate of 
membership to the fund;  
 
(v) Rule 16 by increasing the period from 15 to 45 days for intimating the 
removal/ suspension of a member from the State  roll to the Trustee 
Committee; and, 
 
(vi) Rule 19 by substituting the word 'thiery' with the word 'thirty', thereby 
rectifying a typographical error.”

2. During the course of scrutiny of these Orders, t he Committee has noted 
some cases where there has been a considerable time  lag between the date of 
notification of the Order and the date of its layin g. The annexed statement also 
indicates the period of delay in cases where notifi cations have not been laid as 
per the schedule prescribed by the Committee and wh ere such notifications 
were accompanied by a statement indicating the reasons for the delay in laying. 
In some of the cases the delay has been quite long.  The 
observations/recommendations of the Committee in re spect of the specific 
Ministries/Departments are as follows: -    
  
  

 
(i) Ministry of Agriculture 
 (Department of Agriculture and Cooperation) 
 
Ministry of Agriculture (Department of Agriculture and Cooperation)  
have laid 9 notifications (Sl. Nos. 1 to 9). One notification (Sl. No. 8)  has been 
delayed by 1 year and 1 month with a delay statemen t appended thereto. The 
reasons of delay is given as under:- 
 
 “The above Gazette Notification could not be laid on the Table of both 
the Houses of Parliament inadvertently within the p rescribed period after its 
publication in the Gazette.” 
 
The Committee regrets the inordinate delay in layin g of the 
notification by the Ministry of Agriculture (Depart ment of Agriculture 
and Cooperation) and advise them to take adequate precaution so as to lay 
notifications at the first available opportunity on the Table of the House. 
 
(ii) Ministry of Consumer Affairs 
 (Department of Food and Public Distribution) 
 
 Ministry of Consumer Affairs (Department of Food a nd Public 
Distribution have laid 12 notifications (Sl. Nos. 2 5 to 36). Out of these two  
notifications (Sl. Nos. 25 and 26) have been delaye d. The delay period is of 
about 6 Months and no delay statement is appended thereto. 
  
  The Committee are not happy with the delay in layin g of 
notifications by the Ministry of Consumer Affairs ( Department of Food 
and Public Distribution). The Committee desire that  the Ministry of 
Consumer Affairs  append delay statements where the re is delay in laying 
of notifications and avoid recurrence of such delays in future . 
 
(iii) Ministry of Environment and Forests 
 
 Ministry of Environment and Forests have laid 11 n otifications (Sl. 
Nos. 42 to 52). 3 notifications have been delayed w ith delay period ranging 
from 4 months to 7 months. No delay statement is at tached to any of these 
delayed notifications.  
 
The Committee in the absence of delay statements ar e not able to 
know the reasons behind this delay in laying of not ifications. The 
Committee have clearly mentioned in its 131 
st  Report that delay 
statements should invariably be appended where there is delay in laying of 
notifications. The Committee therefore impress upon  the Ministry to 
strictly adhere to the time schedule as prescribed in Committee’s Report 
that in case of any delay in laying, delay statemen t should invariable be 
appended. 

 
 
(iv) Ministry of External Affairs  
 
 Ministry of External Affairs have laid 4 notificat ions (Sl. Nos. 53 to 
56). 3 notifications have been delayed by 6 months with delay statements 
appended to them. The Ministry have given reason fo r delay as non-
availability of requisite number of printed copies from the Press in time  and 
exigencies of work. 
  
 
 The Committee take serious note of the fact that de lay was caused 
due to non-availability of requisite number of prin ted copies of the 
notifications. Ministries have been taking recourse  to this plea very 
frequently. This possibility  should have been asse ssed well before and 
adequate arrangements should have been made in resp ect thereof. The 
Committee advise the Ministry of External Affairs t o take care in future 
so that such delays do not recur. 
 
 
(v)   Ministry of Finance 
 
(A)  (Department of Economic Affairs) 
 
  The Ministry of Finance (Department of Economic Aff airs) have laid 8 
notifications
 on the Table of the House. Out of these 2 notificat ions have been 
delayed.  One notification (Sl. No. 57) which has b een delayed by 4 months 
and has no delay statements appended thereto. Anoth er notification (Sl. No. 
63) has been accompanied with delay statement. The delay period ranges from 
4 months to one year. The reasons given by the Ministry is under:- 
 
 “The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Terms  and Conditions of 
Service of Chairman and Members) Amendment Rules, 2 009 was published in 
Gazette of India vide S.O, No. 2037 on 23.07.2009. However, the published 
version could not be laid before Rajya Sabha in nex t session due to inadvertent 
error. 
 The delay in laying down the notification in the H ouses of Parliament is 
deeply regretted.” 
 
 The Committee are deeply anguished  over the fact that such 
unreasonable delay was caused inadvertently by the Ministry. The 
Ministry should have kept vigilant to see that noti fications are laid within 
the time schedule prescribed by the Committee. The Committee therefore, 
impress upon the Ministry of Finance (Department of  Economic Affairs) 
to be watchful so that laying is not delayed inadvertently. 
 
 

 
(B)  (Department of Financial Services) 
 
 The Ministry of Finance (Department of Financial S ervices) have laid 
18 notifications (Sl. Nos. 65 – 82). 4 notification s have been delayed. Out of 
these 3 notifications (Sl. Nos. 76, 81 and 82) have  been  delayed from 3 
months to 4 months and have no delay statements att ached to them. One 
notification (Sl. No. 74) has been delayed by 4 mon ths with delay statement 
appended thereto. The reasons forwarded by the Mini stry for delay is as 
under:- 
 
 “The Gazette Notification No. 1/2010 regarding ame ndment in the 
United Bank of India Employees’ Pension  Regulation s 1995 was published in 
the Gazette of India dated July 3 – July 9, 2010. T he Bank has stated that they 
received the copies of Gazette Notification from pr ess on 17.8.2010. The Bank 
has regretted that inadvertently, they could not fu rnish the requisite number of 
copies of Gazette Notification in time. As a result  of this, the said Notification 
could not be laid on the Table of the House during Monsoon Session, 2010 of 
Parliament.” 
 
 The Committee are unhappy to note that delay was c aused 
inadvertently. Ministry of Finance (Department of F inancial Services) 
should ensure timely laying of their notifications as per the schedule 
prescribed in Committee’s 131 
st  Report and any hurdle in timely laying of 
notifications should be instantly done away with.  
 
(C)  (Department of Revenue) 
 
The Ministry of Finance (Department of Revenue) hav e laid 60 
notifications (Sl. Nos. 83 -142). Out of these 7 notifications have been delayed, 
6 notifications have no delay statement appended wi th them and only one 
notification is accompanied with delay statement. T he delay period ranges 
from 3 months to 7 months. The Ministry have given reason for delay as 
under:- 
  
 “Notification No. 30/2010-Customs (NT) dated 8 
th  April, 2010 was 
inadvertently not laid during the last session of t he Parliament and is now 
being laid in the Winter Session of Parliament. The delay may be condoned.” 
  
 The Committee note that the reasons put forth by t he Ministry of 
Finance (Department of Revenue) causing delay in la ying of notifications 
are not convincing. The Committee  is against the c asual approach 
adopted by the Ministry towards laying of notificat ions on the Table of 
Parliament and wish that Ministry would adopt a pro active role in laying 
of notifications in future. 
 
 

 
 
(vi) Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (Departm ent of AYUSH 
sDepartment of Health) 
 
  The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare have laid  2 notifications
 on 
the Table of the House. One of them (Sl. No. 143) h ave been delayed by 5 
months and has no delay statement appended thereto. 
Department of AYUSH has laid only  one notification   and has no 
delay statement appended thereto. The delay period is of 3 months. 
 Department of Health have laid 2 notifications (Sl.  No. 146-147) and 
both of them have been delayed by 3 months and no d elay statement attached 
with them. 
 
 The Committee recommends that the Ministry of Heal th and 
Family Welfare (Department of AYUSH and Department of Health) 
should evolve an effective mechanism to obviate suc h delays and incase of 
delays in laying of notifications, delay statements  should invariably be 
accompanied with them.  
 
(vii)      Ministry of Home Affairs  
 
The Ministry of Home Affairs have laid 57 notifications out of which 
8 notifications have been delayed. The delay period  ranges from 3 months to 4 
months. These notifications (Sl. Nos. 
148, 158-160, 165, 167-168 & 175 ) have no 
delay statement attached.  
 
 The Committee take serious note of the fact that de lay was caused 
due to administrative reasons. Ministries should ha ve taken the matter 
very seriously so that administration reasons do no t come on the way of 
laying. This possibility  should have been assessed  well before and 
adequate arrangements should have been made in resp ect thereof. The 
Committee advise the Ministry of Home Affairs to ta ke care so that such 
delays do not recur in future. 
 
(viii) Ministry of Human Resource Development 
  
 (Department of Higher Education) 
 
Only one  notification that the Ministry of Human R esource 
Development (Department of Higher Education) (Sl. N o. 205) have laid is 
delayed by 10 months and there is no delay statement appended thereto. 
     
  The Committee are not happy over the inordinate del ay in laying 
extending upto 10 months on the part of the Ministr y. Further there is no 
reason given as to what caused this delay. The Comm ittee therefore, 
impress upon  the Ministry to  take care that such instances of delay do 

 
not recur in future and in case of any delay in lay ing,  a delay statement 
should invariably be appended. 
 
(ix) Ministry of Law and Justice 
 
(Department of Justice and Department of Legal Affairs) 
 
The Ministry of Law and Justice (Department of Just ice) have laid 2 
notifications (Sl. Nos. 215-216). Both of them have  been delayed. The delay 
period ranges 1 year and 2 months in one case and 5  years 6 months in the 
other. No delay statement is appended with either of  them. 
 
Department of Legal Affairs have laid 2 notificatio ns. Out of these one 
notification (Sl. No. 217) has been delayed by 1 year and 1 month and no delay 
statement is appended thereto.  
 
 The Committee are surprised at the length of time taken by the 
Ministry of Law and Justice in laying of their noti fications, one by 5 years 
and 6 months and another by one year and one month.  Reasons of this 
exorbitant delay are hard to understand. The Minist ry should stick a 
specific time frame as prescribed by the Committee to lay the 
notifications. The Committee hope that Ministry of Law and Justice 
would take adequate precaution to avoid such instan ces of delay in future 
and would invariable append a delay statement in ca se of delay in laying 
on the Table of the House. 
 
(x) Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pe nsions 
(Department of Personnel and Training) 
 
 The Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and P ensions 
(Department of Personnel and Training)  have laid 29 notifications out of  
which 12 notifications have delayed, 2 notification s (Sl. Nos. 231-232) have 
been delayed by 3 months and have no delay statemen t appended with them. 
10 notifications (Sl. Nos. 221 - 230) have been del ayed by 4 months and have 
delay statements appended with them. The reasons fo r delay given by the 
Ministry is as under:- 
 
 “The notifications was sent to the Government of I ndia Press, Mayapuri 
on 23.07.2010 for publication, but the notification s was printed and published 
by the Press during the fag end of the month of Aug ust, 2010. This is the 
reasons for delay in laying the notifications on th e table of the House during 
the Monsoon Session of the Parliament, 2010 which c ommenced from 26 
th  
July, 2010 and scheduled to end on the 27 th  August, 2010. The delay in laying 
the notifications is regretted.” 
  

 
 The Committee feel that the reply given by the Mini stry is a lame 
excuse. Delay could be avoided, had precaution been  taken by the 
Ministry in this regard. The Committee hope that th e Ministry of 
Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions (Departme nt of Personnel and 
Training) would cut on such delays in future partic ularly on account of 
delay in receiving printed copies of notifications by evolving an effective 
mechanism and would adhere to the time schedule as prescribed in 
Committee’s 131 
st  Report 
 
(xi) Ministry of Power 
 
 Ministry of Power have laid 10 notifications (Sl. Nos. 253 to 262). 
Only one of them (Sl. No. 253) has been delayed by 4 months and is 
accompanied with delay statement. The reasons given  by the Ministry for 
delay is as under:- 
 
 “The notification was published in the Gazette of India Extraordinary 
dated 7 
th  August, 2010, copies of the notification could not be laid on the Rajya 
Sabha before conclusion of the Monsoon Session 2010  as printed copies of the 
same were received by Joint Electricity Regulatory Commission for Goa and 
UTs from the Department of Publication, Ministry of Urban Development on 6 
October, 2010 and Joint Electricity Regulatory Comm ission for Goa and UTs 
forwarded the same to Ministry of Power on 6 th  October, 2010. The Monsoon 
Session concluded on 27 th  August, 2010. Hence the notification is laid on th e 
first opportunity.” 
  
 The Committee is to see that statutory obligation of laying the 
notifications as the Table of House as prescribed b y it is fulfilled by the 
Ministries. It is for the Ministries to see that this job is performed by them 
without flaw. Therefore, Committee urge upon the Mi nistry of Power to 
see to it that hurdles causing delay in laying of n otifications, such as on 
account of receiving printed copies of notification s should be expressly 
removed at their end. 
 
(xii) Ministry of Railways 
 
 (Railway Board) 
  
 The Committee note with regret that the Ministry of Railways (Railway 
Board) have delayed the laying of their only notifi cation (Sl. No. 264) by 6 
months. The delay statement appended by the said notification reads:- 
 
 “Amendment in Schedule II of the RPF Rules, 1987 fo r enhancement 
of power to grant group rewards to RPF personnel, a fter vetting by Ministry of 
Law and Justice, was sent to Government of India Pr ess, Mayapuri, New Delhi 
for publication in Gazette of India, Extra Ordinary. 

 
 
 The Government Press was requested  for printing o f the Gazette 
Notification and sending the printed copies of Gazette Notification to Railways 
Board after publication. 
 
 The copies were not received from the Printing Pre ss. A reminder letter 
was also sent to the Printing Press. A special mess enger was also sent to the 
Printing Press and only after the copies could be collected. 
 
 By the time copies could be collected, the session  was already over, 
Thus, the papers could not be laid in the House in time.” 
 
 The reasons cited by Ministry of Railways i.e. notification could not 
be laid down because the copies of notifications could not be received from 
the Printing Press in time, is not appreciable. It is a Constitutional 
provision to lay the notification within a prescrib ed time schedule and the 
Ministry should have taken appropriate action to la y the same in time on 
the Table of the House. It reflects the bad managem ent planning on the 
part of the Ministry. The Committee therefore, impr ess upon  the 
Ministry to  devise suitable mechanism to avoid suc h instances of delay in 
future particularly on account of delay in receivin g printed copies of 
notifications so as to adhere to the time schedule as prescribed in 
Committee’s 131 
st  Report 
  
(xiii)     Ministry of Road Transport & Highways 
 
 The Ministry of Road Transport & Highways have laid  347 
notifications
 on the Table of the House (Sl. Nos. 265 to 611) 179  notifications 
have been delayed out of which 6 notifications have  accompanied by delay 
statements and 173 notifications have no delay statements appended with them. 
The delay period ranges from 3 months to 1 year 4 m onths. The reasons given 
by the Ministry is that it took some time to comple te the procedural formalities 
and therefore, papers could not be laid in time. 
 
 The Committee appreciate the huge work of laying ha ndled by the 
Ministry of Road Transport and Highways and wish th at Ministry would 
adhere to the time Schedule in laying of notifications . 
  
Delay in framing of Subordinate Legislation 
 
 
(xiv)  In addition to the concern expressed by the Committee over delay 
in laying of Notifications on the Table of the Hous e, the Committee also 
express their deep concern over delay in framing of  rules/regulations 
under different Acts. The Committee in its 47 
th  report presented to the 

 
House on 14.9.1981 has recommended that the rule-ma king process 
should be completed within a period of six months of the coming into force 
on an Act. The committee has further recommended th at in case a 
Ministry is not able to adhere to this time limit, it should seek extension of 
time for completing the rule-making process. The re commendation of the 
committee reads as follows:- 
  “The Committee feels that the rule-making process c ould 
well have been completed within the time limit of s ix months which 
the Committee has laid down for making of rules under an Act after 
coming into force of that Act. Where however, a Min istry does not 
find it possible to adhere to the time limit, they should inform the 
Committee of the reasons why they cannot make rules  within the 
time limit and seek extension of time for completin g the rule-
making process.” 
 The Committee is constrained to take note of the f act that the 
Ministries/Departments of Government of India are n ot complying with 
the Committee’s recommendation to complete the proc ess of framing of 
subordinate legislation contemplated under various Acts of Parliament 
within a period of six months. At the same time, th e Committee also does 
not receive requests for extension of time for comp leting the rule-making 
process in terms of its recommendations as above fr om most of the 
Ministries/Departments. The committee takes a serio us note of the 
prevailing situation in which the Ministries/Depart ments are neither able 
to complete the task of framing rules/regulations u nder different Acts 
within the given six months’ period nor do they suo -motu approach the 
Committee for seeking extension of time. The Commit tee further notes 
that in order to ensure timely framing of rules/reg ulations it has taken an 
initiative to monitor the progress of framing of su bordinate legislation in 
respect of all legislations brought about by differ ent 
Ministries/Departments of Government of India from the year 2003 
onwards with a view to ensure that the framing of s ubordinate legislation 

 
is not delayed. The Committee, however, finds that the responses from the 
Ministries/Departments have not been prompt in this  monitoring exercise 
undertaken on behalf of the Committee.  
 In view of the above position, the Committee once again reiterates 
its recommendation that the Ministries/Departments should ensure 
putting in place subordinate legislation positively  within a period of six 
months of coming into force of the Act. The Committ ee further 
recommends that in case the Ministry fails to meet with this deadline, they 
should invariably approach the Committee for seekin g extension of time. 
The Committee further recommends that in cases wher e the time limit of 
six months is not adhered to, they should, while la ying rules/regulations 
before the Parliament invariably lay a statement ex plaining the reasons 
why the framing of rules/regulations was delayed be yond six months so as 
to keep the Parliament apprised of the compliance o f the Parliament’s 
mandate  conferred upon the Executive. 
  
3. The Committee impresses upon all the Ministries/ Departments to take 
immediate steps to ensure timely and proper laying of subordinate legislation. 
The Committee, accordingly, wishes to bring to the notice of all 
Ministries/Departments of the Government of India, particularly, the defaulting 
ones, the following recommendations, as contained in its 131 
st 
,135 
th  and 152 nd  
Reports: 
 
 “Orders required to be laid before the House shoul d be laid (i) if the 
House is not in Session, during the Session immedia tely following the date 
of publication of the Order in the Official Gazette  and (ii) if the House is 
in Session, on the date of the publication of the O rder, during its 
continuance and in case the time lag between the da te of publication and 
the date of the closing of the Session is less than  15 clear days, before the 
expiry of the Session immediately following the sai d Session. All the 
Ministries/Departments of Government of India shoul d henceforth 
comply with this schedule in the matter of laying o f the Orders issued 
under various Acts of Parliament on the Table of the Rajya Sabha. 
(131 st  Report) 
(Presented on 15 December 2000) 
 

 
 
 “The Committee has, time and again, emphasized tha t it is essential 
that in case there is a delay in the laying of Stat utory Orders, the 
concerned Ministry/Department should invariably app end a delay 
statement along with the notifications being laid s o as to apprise 
Parliament of the causes of delay. The Committee de sires all 
Ministries/Departments to take a note of this, sinc e the intension is that 
through the process of formulation of a delay state ment the Ministry is 
able to introspect, identify bottlenecks and devise remedial measures”. 
(135 th  Report) 
(Presented on 27 July 2001) 
 
 “In the opinion of the Committee, every notificati on should be 
assigned a distinctive number in order to give it a  separate identity and 
similarly, no notification should be published/laid  which does not carry a 
notification number. The Committee expects all Mini stries/Departments 
of Government of India to exercise caution in this regard. In case where 
there are more than one notification under a single  file, the 
Ministries/Departments should ensure that the file number on each 
notification should be suitably distinguished from one another. 
(152 
nd

Report on the  
Building and Other Construction Workers (Regulation of Employment and 
Conditions of Service) Central Rules, 1998  
 
  
 The building and other construction workers are on e of the most vulnerable 
segments of the unorganized sector workers in India. Their work is of a temporary nature.  
Besides, relationship between employer and employee  is also temporary and the working 
hours very uncertain. Basic amenities and welfare f acilities provided to these workers are 
found to be generally inadequate. Nature of work in volved in building and construction 
activities is generally arduous and workmen engaged  therein are prone to frequent 
accidents sometimes leading to death due to absence  of adequate safety measures 
available.  
 
2. Down-sizing and outsourcing have also had a nega tive impact on management of 
health and safety of the workers in construction industry. Informal contractual conditions, 
fear of losing employment makes it further difficul t for construction workers to exercise 
their rights.  Often, time and financial constrains  compel employers to ignore the health 
and safety of workers even if that results in their death. 
 
3. Keeping in view the above circumstances the Buil ding and other Construction 
Workers (Regulation of Employment and Conditions of  Service) Act, 1996 was enacted 
by the Parliament to regulate the employment and co nditions of service of building and 
other construction workers and to provide for their  safety and welfare measures. The  
Building and other Construction Workers (Regulation  of Employment and Conditions of 
Service) Rules, 1998 ( Annexure I ) framed under the above Act were taken up for 
examination by the Committee keeping in view its importance in July, 1999. 
 
4. The Committee discussed the subject with the rep resentatives of the National 
Building Construction Corporation Ltd. (NBCC) and t he Ministries of Urban 
Development and Labour and Employment on 22 
nd  October, 1999 at New Delhi for 
eliciting requisite inputs on the subject matter. D uring the course of the discussion, the 
Committee was apprised of the fact that even though  the construction workers were 
covered to some extent by various labour laws, but being a special category of workers it 

was felt to have a separate legislation for them. D uring the discussion the Ministry of 
Labour accepted the fact that the implementation machinery with respect to the Act/Rules 
was inadequate and needed to be strengthened. Furth er the Committee was informed that 
“other Construction Workers” included workers in co nstruction areas like power 
generator, transmission, distribution, gas installa tions, communications, etc, and since 
they were exposed to same hazards risks and problem s which the building workers faced, 
therefore, these category of workers had also been included under the purview of the Act. 
A study note on the discussions held during the meeting was prepared. (Annexure -II) 
 
5. The Committee, thereafter considered the matter at its meeting held on 20 
th  June, 
2000 and desired to know the reasons for delay in the framing of rules under the Building 
and Other Construction Workers Employment Act, 1996  and continuing delay in 
implementation of the provisions of the Act and the  rules. Accordingly, a reference was 
made to the Ministry of Labour and Employment seeki ng their comments on the above 
points on 5 th  July, 2000. The Ministry furnished their comments on the 2 nd  August, 2000. 
The points referred to the Ministry and their comments/clarifications received thereon are 
reproduced below:- 
I. Point referred  
 Regarding delay in the framing of the rules under the Building and Other 
Construction Workers Employment Act, 1996.  
 
Ministry's comments (2.8.2000)  
 In conformity with Section 5(1) of the Act, the gov ernment constituted an Expert 
Committee on the 17 
th  May, 1996 under the Chairmanship of Joint Secretar y/director 
General (Labour Welfare). The other members of the Committee were Director General, 
Factory Advice Service and labour Institute, Labour  Secretary, Government of Kerala, 
Chief Labour Commissioner (C), Chief Engineer (Vigi lance), Central Public Works 
Department and Executive Director, Civil Engineerin g (General), Ministry of Railways. 
Its constitution was revised in November, 1996. The  Expert Committee met on the 20 th  
August, 1996 and constituted two sub-groups for the purpose of drafting the rules-one for 
the purpose of general rules and other for the purp ose of health and safety rules. The 
Committee met again on the 4 th  February, 1997. In the subsequent meeting held on the 

26 th  March, 1997 the draft rules prepared by the sub-gr oups were amalgamated and 
approved. Since offices of the members of the Committee were located at different places 
i.e. Delhi, Mumbai and Thiruvananthapuram and the rules were voluminous and technical 
in nature, it took long time for the Committee to subject the draft report. Further, the rules 
required extensive consultation and discussion between the Ministries of Law and Justice, 
and Labour and Employment before they were finally vetted by the Ministry of Law and 
Justice in October, 1998 and notified on the 19 th  November, 1998. 
 
II. Point referred  
 Regarding the continuing delay in implementation o f the provisions of the Act 
and the Rules. 
 
Ministry's comments (2.8.2000)  
 The implementation of the provisions of the Act (s ) is to be expedited by the 
States and Union Territories. The status report reg arding implementation of the Act by 
the State Governments has already been furnished to  the Rajya Sabha Secretariat vide 
O.M of even number dated the 31 
st  March, 2000. Minister of State for Labour and 
Employment has also written to the Labour Ministrie s of all States in this regard. The 
Government also propose to hold a Conference of the  Labour Ministers of the States so 
as to emphasize the need for speedy implementation of the Act and to have first hand 
information regarding difficulties, if any, in the implementation of the Act (s).  
 
6. Thereafter, the Committee discussed the subject matter with the representatives of 
the Oil and Natural Gas Corporation Limited (ONGC) and the Ministry of Petroleum and 
Natural Gas and Ministry of Labour & Employment on the 29 
th  September, 2000, at 
Mumbai. During the course of the discussion, supple mentary questionnaires were handed 
over to the Oil and Natural Gas Corporation, Minist ry of Petroleum & Natural Gas and 
Ministry of Labour and Employment for their comment s/ clarifications. Relevant extracts 
from the study note on the above meeting is enclose d (Annexure  III).  A brief review of 
the comments received is reproduced in the succeeding paragraphs. 
 

7. The Committee raised the issue as to why the reg istration of the workers had been 
made optional. The Ministry of Labour and Employmen t commented that the objectives 
of the Act are to take care of the health and safet y of the workers and provide certain 
social security and welfare measures. For this purp ose there is a provision of constitution 
of State Building and Other Construction Workers’ W elfare Board. To undertake the 
social security and welfare measures, a Building and other Construction Workers Welfare 
Fund is to be constituted. There is a provision of levy of a cess on the cost of construction 
and also contribution from the beneficiaries regist ered with the Board. The health and 
safety provisions are applicable to all the workers irrespective of the fact whether they are 
registered with the Board or not. Since there is a provision of contribution to the Fund 
from the workers with the objective to create a sen se of participation, the registration has 
been made optional and not mandatory or obligatory.  
 
8. The Committee also sought clarification arising out of the definition “employer” 
which means owner and includes contractor in relati on to a building or other construction 
work carried on through a contractor or by the empl oyment of building workers supplied 
by the contractor. The Committee wanted to know if work is done by a contractor who 
has to comply with the provisions of the Act/Rules,  whether the owner will also be liable 
in such case, and, if so, what are the reasons for making both the owner and contractor 
liable simultaneously. 
 
9. The Ministry of Labour explained that section 2( 1) of the Act defines “employer.” 
Section 2(1) (iii) further defines that: 
“In relation to a building or other construction wo rk carried on by 
or through a contractor, or by the employment of bu ilding workers 
supplied by a contractor, the contractor” 
 
In view of above provisions of the Act, where contr actor is the employer, the 
responsibility to comply with the provisions of the Act is that of the contractor. However, 
to safeguard the interest of the workers in so far as payment of wages and compensation 
is concerned, the employer has been made liable to ensure payment of full wages by the 
contractor in the matter as specified under section  45 of the Act and Rule 5 (10) of the 
Rules framed under the Act. 

 
10. The Committee expressed apprehension on the con tradiction between Rule 9 
in relation to its observation that the Act did not contemplate any kind of exemption 
from the provisions of the Act.  The Ministry of La bour and Employment informed 
that the Act and Rules made thereunder did not prov ide exemption to certain 
categories of establishments from the implementatio n of the Act.  Under Rule 9, the 
exemption is contemplated in respect of applicability of Rules and not the provisions 
of the Act and that too when this does not affect t he safety, health and welfare of the 
building workers.  However, the Ministry submitted that the matter could be 
examined in consultation with the Law Ministry.   
 
11. The Committee again discussed the matter with t he representatives of the 
State Government of Kerala and the Ministry of Labo ur and Employment at 
Cochin on the 19 
th  January, 2001.  Relevant extracts from the study n ote (Annexure-
IV)  on the above discussion were forwarded to the Mini stry of Labour and 
Employment for necessary action on the 15 th  February, 2001. 
 
12. The Ministry of Labour and Employment vide  their  communication dated 
the 30 
th  April, 2001 expressed their stand on all points ex cept on Rule 9 of the 
Central Rules.  The Ministry informed that the conc erned Ministries/Departments 
had been requested to register under the Building a nd Other Construction Workers 
(Regulation of Employment & Conditions of Service) Act, 1996 and pay cess to the 
Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Boa rds constituted under the 
Act.  Further, the State Governments had also been requested to expedite 
implementation of the said Act and frame State Rule s, constitute the State Advisory 
Committee, the Welfare Fund and to notify the authorities under the Act.  A copy of 
the Rules framed by the Government of Kerala under the Act was also sent to the 
State Governments for necessary action at their end .  Regarding the matter of Rule 
9 of the Central Rules relating to power of the Gov ernment to exempt from 
applicability all or any requirements of the Rules,  the matter was being examined in 
consultation with the Legal Department. 
 

13. Thereafter, after a couple of interim replies, the Ministry on the 8 th  April, 
2003 clarified their position as follows:- 
 
 “It is stated that an interim reply has been sent t o the Rajya Sabha Secretariat 
vide this Ministry’s O.M. of even number dated the 30 
th  April, 2001 wherein it 
has been communicated that the matter of Rule 9 of the Central Rules relating 
to the powers to the Government to exempt from all or any requirements of the 
Rules, was being examined in consultation with the Ministry of Law and 
Justice, Legislative Department. 
Now the Legislative Department has stated that Rule  9 of the Building and 
Other Construction Workers (Regulation of Employment & Conditions of 
Service) Rules 1998 exempts any building or any appliance fr om all or any of 
the provisions of the said Rule and does not confer powers to the Government to 
exempt any of the provisions of the Main Act i.e., Building and Other 
Construction Workers (Regulation of Employment & Co nditions of Service) 
Act, 1996.  Clarifying the point further they opine d that similar exemption 
powers have been provided in Rule 16 of the Coir In dustries (Registration and 
Licensing) Rules, 1958 even though the principal Ac t namely the Coir 
Industries Act, 1958 does not contain any provision s for giving exemption.  
Hence, it is felt that technically there is no cont radiction of the provisions of 
Rule 9 of Building and Other Construction Workers ( RECS) Rules, 1998 in 
relation to provisions of the main Act”. 
     
14. The Committee took up the matter for further co nsideration on the 5 
th  September 
2005. It decided to seek updated information on the  subject by making a reference to the 
Ministry, which, accordingly, was made on the 28 th  December 2005. Thereafter, the 
Ministry vide  their communication dated the 17 th  January, 2006 furnished their position 
as follows:- 
“(i)  Number of construction Projects/Units of the Central Ministries/Departments 
which have been registered under the Building and O ther Construction 
Workers (RECS) Act, 1996 by the concerned Appropria te Governments 
through out the country are not maintained in the Ministry. 
 
(ii) Status of implementation of the above Act in the St ates/UTs as on 
31.12.2005 . 
 

(iii) Rule 9 of the Building and Other Construction Worke rs (RECS) Central 
Rules, 1998 have been formulated keeping in view th e arrangements 
existing/made by the employers/contractors at the c onstruction site.  
Further, the Government shall not grant exemption under this rule unless it 
is satisfied that such exemption would not adversel y affect the safety, 
health and wealth of the building workers”.  
 
  15. The Committee considered the matter in its me eting held on 7 
th  June, 2006.  The 
Committee observed that the Building and Other Cons truction Workers (Regulations of 
Employment and Condition of Service) Central Rules,  1998 was an important piece of 
legislation and covered a vast area.  But there was a continuing delay in implementing the 
provisions of the concerned Act and the Rules.  The  Committee, accordingly, decided to 
hear the Secretary, Ministry of Labour and Employme nt for seeking clarifications on 
some of the points that had come up during the course of examination of the Rules.  
 
 16 The Committee heard the views of the Secretary,  Ministry of Labour and 
Employment at New Delhi on the 17 th  August, 2009.  During the meeting, the 
Chairperson expressed the Committee’s concern over the continuing delay in the 
implementation of provisions of the Act and the Rul es, by the States and the Union 
Territories. The Committee also expressed its reser vation over the poor implementation 
and poor monitoring by the Central Government despi te elaborate provisions in the Act. 
The Committee also sought to know if the contract l abourers, who form a sizable 
segment of labourers in such projects, were covered  under these Rules. The Committee 
took note of the fact that in several States not a single labourer was registered, the 
collection of Welfare Cess was much below the estim ates and its utilisation by the 
appropriate Government for the welfare of the labou rers has been rather dismal. The 
Committee recognized that in a few States the cess was being collected without 
constituting the Boards. Concern was expressed over  the exploitation of contract 
labourers by the labour contractor, who did not pay  even the minimum wages. The 
Committee also found the figures of registered labo urers in Delhi unrealistically low. It 
was submitted by the Secretary, Department of Labou r, Government of National Capital 
Territory of Delhi, that as per a recent survey, th e estimated number of labourers in Delhi 
stood at 4.5 lakhs. The Chairperson sought to know if labourers were actually being paid 
the pension as provided in the Act.  
 
17. The Secretary, Ministry of Labour, informed the Committee that the provisions of the 
Rules were aimed to protect the service conditions of the unskilled migrant labourers 
engaged in the building and other construction acti vities. The Committee sought to know 
the implementation of these Rules in the Central Go vernment projects in Delhi like the 
Delhi Metro Rail and projects relating to Commonwea lth Games.  It was clarified that 
while the Central Government retained the power of enforcing the Rules, the welfare of 
labourers is to be implemented by the respective St ate Governments. The Secretary, 
Ministry of Labour and Employment, agreed with the Committee’s impression that the 
implementation of the Rules was far from being satisfactory. 
 

18. Thereafter, the Committee held discussions with  the representatives of Ministry of 
Labour and Employment and Department of Labour of t he Government of NCT of Delhi 
alongwith the representatives of National Building Construction Company Ltd. (NBCC), 
Central Public Works Department (CPWD), Delhi Metro  Rail Corporation (DMRC), 
IRCON, Delhi Development Authority (DDA), Housing a nd Urban Development 
Corporation Limited (HUDCO), National Projects Cons truction Corporation Limited 
(HUDCO) and Hindustan Prefab Limited on 28 th  August, 2009. During the course of the 
discussion the Committee noted the fact due to non- existence of Boards and 
programmes/schemes in the States the concerned agencies were not able to transfer funds 
that they collected as cess amount. A study note on  the discussions was also prepared. 
(Annexure-V) . 
 
19. The Committee also took up for discussion the s aid Rules with  Neyveli Lignite 
Corporation Limited, Bharat Heavy Electricals Limit ed, National Highways Authority of 
India along with the representatives of the State Government of Tamil Nadu and Ministry 
of Labour and Employment at Chennai on 22 
nd  December, 2010 . The Committee was 
informed that in Tamil Nadu welfare schemes framed under the Tamil Nadu Manual 
Workers (Regulation of Employment and Conditions of  Work) Act, 1982 were being 
implemented.  The reason for this was that Section 63 of the Building and Other 
Construction Workers (Regulation of Employment and Conditions of Service) Act, 1996 
provides that the said Act would not affect the ope ration of any corresponding law in a 
State if the welfare schemes under it are more bene ficial to the building and other 
construction workers than those provided under the Central Act. However the Committee 
noted that some of the organizations were not payin g the cess contemplated under the 
State Act. The Committee was of the opinion that th e concerned stake holders should 
resolve the issue of collection of cess under the S tate Act at the earliest so that the rights 
of the workers are not lost . A study note on the discussion was also prepared. 
(Annexure-VI) 
 
General observations and recommendations of the Committee  
 

20. The Committee during the course of its discussi ons with the concerned 
Ministries and other organisatons associated with t he implementation of the Rules 
observed the following facts: 
 
21. The Committee expressed its dismay over the fac t that even after the 
Building and other Construction Workers (Regulation  of Employment and 
Conditions of Service) Act, 1996  and the Building and other Construction Workers 
(Regulation of Employment and Conditions of Service ) Rules, 1998  have been in 
operation for a sufficiently long time, the States have shown a general reluctance to 
implement the welfare measures in its true spirit.  This is evident from the data 
submitted by the Ministry of Labour and Employment.   As per the statistics, States 
like Chattisgarh, Jharkhand, Rajasthan, Uttar Prade sh and others have not even 
registered a single worker under the Act. However, on the other hand, the 
Committee appreciates the efforts made by States li ke Kerela and Tamil Nadu in 
getting the registration of workers done. The Commi ttee therefore, recommends 
that a time frame should be decided and progress ma de by States be monitored 
regularly. The Committee hope that the Central Advi sory Committee would ensure 
all States take adequate steps to implement the Rul es. The Committee is also of the 
view that the Ministry of Labour has two models bef ore it, one operational in 
Kerala and other in Tamil Nadu. The Committee there fore recommends that the 
Ministry should examine both the models and see if any improvements in the 
existing provisions can be made at Central or State levels. 
 
22. The Committee observed that the registration pr ocess was lengthy and the 
paper work involved discouraged the workers, majori ty of whom were illiterate and 
migrant.  It felt that the duty attendance register  could be used to issue certificates 
and to register the workers.  The Committee, theref ore, recommends that the paper 
work involved should be reduced to the minimum and steps be taken to ensure 
adequate publicity to the Rules. The feasibility of  issuing identity cards with all 
India validity should also be studied and if possible be implemented. The Committee 
appreciates the proposal to extend Rashtriya Swasth ya Bima Yojana to Building 
and Other Construction Workers as it is a progressi ve step and hopes steps would 

be taken to ensure its success. The district labour  inspectors should also undertake 
field trips and register workers on the spot.  The concerned agencies should also be 
motivated to generate awareness about the rules amo ngst the workers as also to 
facilitate the registration so that they were covered under the rule for availing of the 
benefits. 
 
23. During the course of the discussions the fact c ame up time and again that a 
number of States have still to frame welfare scheme s for the workers as 
contemplated under the Act. This had on a number of  occasions led to situation 
where the concerned agencies had deposited the cess  collected by them but it was 
lying ideal in the absence of welfare schemes which  the concerned State 
Governments have to frame. The Committee expresses its concern over the issue 
and hopes that the Ministry would make efforts to p ersuade the States to take 
suitable time bound steps in this regard. The Commi ttee also suggests that the 
Ministry could frame Welfare Schemes which the Stat es can adopt with suitable 
modifications. 
 
24.  The Committee notes that now a days developmen t of infrastructure has led 
to lots of construction activity, both in the priva te and public sector. These projects 
involve large number of construction workers and th e well being of these workers is 
a cause of concern. The Committee, therefore, recom mends that special 
measures/mechanism be put in place to ensure adequa te implementation of the 
welfare measures contemplated for them under the Ru les. Measures like awareness 
programmes for the workers may be organized to help  them gain knowledge about 
their rights. 
 
25.   The Committee expresses its concern about the  occupational diseases 
effecting the health of the workers and the need fo r ensuring adequate provisions to 
be made to protect the workers from such occupation al diseases. The Committee, 
therefore, recommends that the Rules should also pr ovide for safety measures to 
prevent such occupational diseases and provision fo r their treatment in case the 
worker gets affected.   

 
26. The Committee has also noted that some of the o rganizations are not paying 
the cess contemplated under the State Act. The Comm ittee, therefore, recommends 
that the concerned stake holders should resolve the  issue of collection of cess under 
the State Act at the earliest so that the rights of the workers are not lost.

INTRODUCTION 
 
 
1. I, the Chairman of the Committee on Subordinate Legislation, having been 
authorized by the Committee, do hereby present on i ts behalf, this One Hundred and
